item.text: {"question_id":"2B.10","answer":"For López Obrador’s 2023 period, the supplied record supports a mixed and limited conclusion rather than a demonstrated durable international peace legacy. Mexico publicly condemned Russia’s invasion, advocated peaceful dispute resolution and mediation, participated in Colombia’s peace dialogue, hosted Venezuelan negotiations, and maintained important North American cooperation (BATCH-0045-E012; BATCH-0048-E014; BATCH-0051-E020). These are attributable diplomatic positions and engagements, but the evidence does not establish that the proposed mediation produced a settlement, that declared commitments were fully implemented, or that López Obrador created durable international peace institutions. Bilateral relations also combined continued trade and cooperation with disputes, strained security cooperation, and external constraints (BATCH-0051-E020). The domestic-security evidence should be treated only as contextual and not as the international end-state: Mexico’s peacefulness improved 1.4% in 2023, homicides fell 5.3%, and armed confrontations and some serious rights violations declined in absolute terms, while organized-crime violence remained severe, peace remained 14.4% worse than in 2015, and political violence reached a record (BATCH-0004-E019; BATCH-0047-E009). The administration’s expansion and attempted entrenchment of militarized security institutions, alongside contested accountability and weakened civilian oversight, qualifies any claim that the period strengthened lawful, durable security institutions, although these findings concern primarily domestic security and cannot by themselves establish an international judgment (BATCH-0016-E002; BATCH-0016-E006; BATCH-0047-E009; BATCH-0047-E011). Overall, the evidence shows diplomatic restraint and some constructive international engagement amid inherited insecurity, bilateral dependence, and limited demonstrated authority over external outcomes, but no verified durable international settlement or clearly improved lawful international end-state.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0045-E012","BATCH-0048-E014","BATCH-0051-E020","BATCH-0004-E019","BATCH-0047-E009"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E002","BATCH-0016-E006","BATCH-0047-E011","BATCH-0051-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence documents diplomatic positions and hosting or participation in dialogue, but not a completed López Obrador-era international settlement attributable to him.","International conflict exposure and direct causal authority over external outcomes are limited in the supplied record; North American outcomes also reflected bilateral and structural constraints.","Domestic-security indicators are not decisive international-peace evidence and are included only as contextual qualification regarding lawful institutional durability.","Several adverse institutional conclusions are analytical or opinion evidence rather than judicial findings; the record is also limited on implementation, proxy control, and independent accountability in international conduct."] ,"corrections_made":["Removed the draft’s treatment of domestic insecurity as the central adverse international end-state.","Replaced unsupported claims of lawful diplomatic commitments and continuity with narrower descriptions of documented positions, proposals, and engagements.","Added contrary evidence on 2023 improvement in peacefulness, homicide decline, fewer armed confrontations, and reduced absolute levels of some serious rights violations.","Preserved adverse institutional and accountability evidence only with explicit domestic-scope and source-quality qualifications.","Clarified that no durable settlement or verified international end-state improvement is demonstrated."] ,"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A fuller ledger could clarify whether Mexico’s diplomatic initiatives produced implemented confidence-building measures or settlements.","Additional evidence is needed on international-security decisions, arms or proxy responsibilities, legal compliance, and independent accountability during the target period.","The domestic-security material should be reweighted or omitted if the full ledger contains stronger directly international evidence."]}
